title: Book Three · Chapter 17: The Red Box
story:
At the end of the next week, another letter comes from Leo.

Ronan opens it after dinner. Outside, Mum is taking her dry washing from the line. Dad is putting the dinner bowls away.

Leo's first line is about the square.

I found fourteen. Then I drew some more lines. I stopped at twenty and went to eat.

Ronan laughs. Below the words is a square full of lines. Some are crooked.

Then Leo answers the questions about the shop.

The man sells bowls and cups. The red box is empty. He uses it as a little table. The cups stand on top.

“What is funny?” Dad asks.

“I thought there was something special in a box. It is empty.”

Dad dries his hands and comes over.

“Whose box?”

“The man outside Leo's window.”

Ronan tells him about the morning boxes. Dad looks at the drawing, then goes to the kitchen for his tea.

Ronan reads the rest. Leo has a new place to play after school. His aunt wants him home before dinner. Last week, he stayed too long and ate cold rice.

The next lines are small and close together.

My aunt makes good soup. Cold rice is still cold rice. I go home earlier now.

There is a little cup beside Leo's name. Its handle is bigger than the cup.

Mum comes in with the washing. Ronan moves his school bag off the spare chair.

“He got the square,” he tells her.

“All of it?”

“Fourteen squares. Then he made a new one.”

Mum puts the clothes on the chair. She takes out one of Ronan's shirts and checks a loose button.

“This needs a few stitches.”

“Can I do it?”

She looks at him.

“Yes. Get the small needle case.”

Ronan puts the letter back in its envelope. Mum gives him a needle and some thread. He sits beside her at the table.

The thread misses the needle's eye twice. On the third try, he gets it through.

Mum shows him the first stitch. He makes the next one slowly. The button turns under his fingers.

“Hold it flat,” she says.

He tries again. This stitch stays where he wants it.

Dad comes back with his cup. He watches for a moment.

“Is that my shirt?”

“Mine,” Ronan says.

“Good. I need mine tomorrow.”

Mum laughs. Ronan looks up from the button.

“I need mine too.”

“Then finish before tomorrow.”

When the button is firm, Mum shows him the knot. He cuts the thread and holds up the shirt.

The button sits a little higher than before. It still goes through the hole.

He puts the shirt away. Then he lays Leo's new letter beside the first one in his drawer.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

crooked＝歪的；stitch＝针脚、缝一针；needle's eye＝针眼；knot＝结。

## 理解问题

1. Leo窗外的红箱子实际用来做什么？他为什么开始早点回姨妈家？
2. Ronan读信之后学着做了什么？谁教他，最后能不能使用？

## 读句子

**Mum gives him a needle and some thread.**

拆开看：Mum / gives him / a needle and some thread.

Mum／给他／一根针和一些线。
